```{=html}
<h2 class="gw-eyebrow">The Research</h2>
```

::: gw-prose
### How do local agencies account for water under land use alternatives, and how do they involve communities?
:::

```{=html}
<div class="gw-pinned gw-pinned--prose" data-pinned style="--runway: 240vh">
  <div class="gw-pinned__stage">
    <div class="gw-pinned__viewport">
      <ol class="gw-pinned__track">
        <li class="gw-pinned__step" data-num="01">
          <p>Under the Sustainable Groundwater Management Act, an agency must
          define what unsustainable looks like, measure whether it is happening,
          and act when it is. Each of those steps needs a defined method and
          number. These methods and numbers do not need to be the same across
          basins.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="gw-pinned__step" data-num="02">
          <p>This analysis starts by combing through the literature to get a
          sense of what documented approaches already exist. It gives an idea of
          the scientific ways in which depletion of surface water from pumping is
          quantified, benefits of land repurposing are evaluated, and community
          considerations are equitably incorporated.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="gw-pinned__step" data-num="03">
          <p>Then the analysis looks toward policy and planning documents at the
          local level to find out whether these approaches are being adopted into
          management — and if not, what is happening instead.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="gw-pinned__step" data-num="04">
          <p>Comparing and contrasting these findings between the literature and
          policy, as well as across groundwater subbasins, sheds light on the
          current practices and gaps that exist within groundwater accounting
          frameworks.</p>
        </li>
      </ol>
    </div>
    <div class="gw-pinned__progress" role="group" aria-label="Jump to item">
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Paragraph 1"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Paragraph 2"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Paragraph 3"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Paragraph 4"></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<script type="module" src="assets/js/pinned-scene.js"></script>
```

::: {.gw-band .gw-band--sage}
::: {.gw-page}

```{=html}
<h2 class="gw-eyebrow">Headline findings</h2>

<div class="gw-pinned gw-pinned--headlines" data-pinned style="--runway: 350vh">
  <div class="gw-pinned__stage">
    <span class="gw-pinned__num" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
    <div class="gw-pinned__viewport">
      <ol class="gw-pinned__track gw-headlines">

        <li class="gw-pinned__step gw-headline" data-num="01">
          <h3>Measurement is more sophisticated than accounting</h3>
          <p>All three subbasins run numerical groundwater–surface water models of
          the same generation, and all three produce a pumping-attributable
          depletion figure. In every case the compliance loop closes on a
          groundwater-level proxy instead — not on any measured or modeled
          depletion quantity. None attaches a numeric uncertainty range to an ISW
          figure.</p>
          <p class="gw-headline__meta">
            <span>Chapter 1 · Interconnected Surface Water</span>
            <a href="findings.html?chapter=1.%20ISW&amp;section=1.8%20Gaps%20and%20Uncertainty">See the evidence &rarr;</a>
          </p>
        </li>

        <li class="gw-pinned__step gw-headline" data-num="02">
          <h3>Verification is the missing middle of land repurposing</h3>
          <p>The three programs differ less in what they fund than in when they
          count. One measures water use on repurposed parcels after implementation
          and treats the result as enforceable. One estimates savings beforehand
          and never compares the estimate to anything after. One holds its
          measurement outside the accounting system entirely. None runs a paired
          comparison of expected against measured savings on an enrolled parcel.</p>
          <p class="gw-headline__meta">
            <span>Chapter 2 · Land Repurposing</span>
            <a href="findings.html?chapter=2.%20MLRP&amp;section=2.2%20Verification%20triggers">See the evidence &rarr;</a>
          </p>
        </li>

        <li class="gw-pinned__step gw-headline" data-num="03">
          <h3>Allocation rules decide whether a saving stays saved</h3>
          <p>Changing the land use and changing the entitlement to pump are
          separate design decisions. Across the three programs the entitlement
          variously stays with the landowner and can move, is suspended for the
          paid term with no transfer mechanism, or ceases to exist because the land
          was bought outright. None of the three publishes reporting on the
          allocation status of repurposed parcels, so none could detect movement
          even where movement is permitted.</p>
          <p class="gw-headline__meta">
            <span>Chapter 2 · Land Repurposing</span>
            <a href="findings.html?chapter=2.%20MLRP&amp;section=2.3%20Allocation%20and%20Leakage">See the evidence &rarr;</a>
          </p>
        </li>

        <li class="gw-pinned__step gw-headline" data-num="04">
          <h3>Community equity is not one variable</h3>
          <p>Representative, procedural, and distributional equity move
          independently. The subbasin with the strongest formal representation
          qualifies it with a supermajority voting rule; the two without a
          comparable seat differ from each other on fees, standing, and appeal
          timelines. Distributional outcomes are the gap shared by all three — and
          not for want of data. Every basin holds the well records, published
          thresholds, and community boundaries the analysis would need.</p>
          <p class="gw-headline__meta">
            <span>Chapter 3 · Community</span>
            <a href="findings.html?chapter=3.%20Community%20Considerations&amp;section=3.1.3%20Procedural%20%2F%20Distributional%20%2F%20Representative">See the evidence &rarr;</a>
          </p>
        </li>

        <li class="gw-pinned__step gw-headline" data-num="05">
          <h3>The literature–practice gap runs both ways</h3>
          <p>For several outcomes — per-well depletion attribution, ecological
          co-benefit quantification, domestic-well impact estimation — methods
          exist in the literature and appear nowhere in the reviewed document sets.
          But not every gap is an unused method. For field-scale dust accounting
          and for a unit of community benefit, the literature is empty too: those
          would have to be built rather than adopted.</p>
          <p class="gw-headline__meta">
            <span>Cross-cutting</span>
            <a href="findings.html?db=literature">Explore the literature &rarr;</a>
          </p>
        </li>

      </ol>
    </div>
    <div class="gw-pinned__progress" role="group" aria-label="Jump to item">
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Finding 1"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Finding 2"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Finding 3"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Finding 4"></button>
      <button type="button" class="gw-pinned__dot" aria-label="Finding 5"></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<script type="module" src="assets/js/pinned-scene.js"></script>
```

::: gw-caption
The three document sets are not equally complete — some Salinas Valley
absences are gaps in document availability, some East Turlock absences reflect
programs that have not yet produced results. Across this site, "not found in
reviewed documents" means exactly that, never that a practice does not exist.
:::

```{=html}
<h2 class="gw-eyebrow" style="color:var(--sand)">Analysis Pipeline</h2>
```

```{=html}
<figure class="gw-figure gw-pipeline">
  <div class="gw-figure__body">
    <div class="gw-flow" role="img" aria-labelledby="workflow-summary">
      <p id="workflow-summary" class="gw-sr-summary">
        Workflow diagram in three labelled bands. Information Sources: an academic
        literature review and a review of basin policy and planning documents feed
        the analysis; a third source, GSA board meetings, is registered but not
        yet reviewed. Information Extraction: structured finding extraction records
        each finding with its document, section, quotation, and source location,
        applying the same {{< var comparison_questions_total >}}-question comparison frame to every subbasin; findings
        are then classified and their quotations verified. Synthesis: the coded
        findings are compared across basins and turned into implications for the
        groundwater accounting platform and for DWR.
      </p>

      <div class="gw-pipeline__group">
        <span class="gw-pipeline__glabel">Information Sources</span>
        <div class="gw-pipeline__row gw-pipeline__row--3">
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <span class="gw-pipeline__icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 6c-1.6-1.1-3.7-1.5-6-1.5v13c2.3 0 4.4.4 6 1.5 1.6-1.1 3.7-1.5 6-1.5v-13c-2.3 0-4.4.4-6 1.5Z"/><path d="M12 6v13"/></svg></span>
            <strong>Academic literature</strong>
            <span>Methods demonstrated in the published literature</span>
          </div>
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <span class="gw-pipeline__icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M7 3h7l4 4v14H7z"/><path d="M14 3v4h4M10 12h5M10 16h5"/></svg></span>
            <strong>Policy &amp; planning documents</strong>
            <span>Plans, amendments, rules, evaluations, annual reports, program instruments, comments</span>
          </div>
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node gw-pipeline__node--planned">
            <span class="gw-pipeline__icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="9" cy="8" r="2.5"/><circle cx="16" cy="9" r="2"/><path d="M4 18c0-2.8 2.2-5 5-5s5 2.2 5 5M14 17c.3-2 1.9-3.5 4-3.5s3.7 1.5 4 3.5"/></svg></span>
            <strong>GSA board meetings</strong>
            <span>Registered as a future source. Not yet reviewed — contributes nothing to this site.</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="gw-pipeline__arrow" aria-hidden="true">&darr;</div>

      <div class="gw-pipeline__group">
        <span class="gw-pipeline__glabel">Information Extraction</span>
        <div class="gw-pipeline__row gw-pipeline__row--1">
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <strong>Structured finding extraction</strong>
            <span>Each finding is recorded with its document, section, direct
            quotation, and source location. The same {{< var comparison_questions_total >}}-question
            comparison frame is applied to every subbasin — {{< var comparison_questions_all_basins >}}
            questions answered for all three, the rest for two or more — so adding
            a subbasin means answering the same questions again, not redesigning
            the analysis.</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="gw-pipeline__arrow" aria-hidden="true">&darr;</div>
        <div class="gw-pipeline__row gw-pipeline__row--2">
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <strong>Classification</strong>
            <span>Positive, absence, or ambiguous; relevance to the accounting platform and to DWR recommendations</span>
          </div>
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <strong>Quote verification</strong>
            <span>Quotations checked against the source document</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="gw-pipeline__arrow" aria-hidden="true">&darr;</div>

      <div class="gw-pipeline__group">
        <span class="gw-pipeline__glabel">Synthesis</span>
        <div class="gw-pipeline__row gw-pipeline__row--2">
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <strong>Cross-basin comparison</strong>
            <span>The same question asked of each subbasin, compared answer by answer</span>
          </div>
          <div class="gw-pipeline__node">
            <strong>Platform and policy implications</strong>
            <span>What the pattern implies for a groundwater accounting platform and for DWR guidance</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</figure>
```
